claims.text: High-temperature synthesis promotes complete atomic mixing in noble metal–based HEA nanomaterials.
Complete atomic mixing produces uniform electronic environments.
Complete atomic mixing produces uniform strain environments.
Complete atomic mixing promotes formation of a stable, single-phase alloy.
A homogeneous alloy phase optimizes adsorption of catalytic reaction intermediates.
Optimized intermediate adsorption increases catalytic activity and selectivity.
Lower-temperature synthesis can leave kinetic barriers to alloy homogenization unovercome.
Lower-temperature synthesis leads to elemental clustering or phase segregation.
Elemental clustering or phase segregation disrupts catalytically active-site ensembles.
Disruption of active-site ensembles degrades catalytic performance.
High-temperature synthesis increases configurational entropy.
High-temperature synthesis overcomes kinetic barriers and produces a uniform distribution of noble metal atoms.
A uniform atomic distribution tailors local electronic structure and surface strain.
Tailored local electronic structure and surface strain optimize adsorption energies of key reaction intermediates.
High-temperature samples will have more uniform atomic distributions than lower-temperature samples.
High-temperature samples will have less local strain inhomogeneity than lower-temperature samples.
High-temperature samples will exhibit greater catalytic activity than lower-temperature samples.
High-temperature samples will exhibit better catalytic selectivity than lower-temperature samples.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold when constituent elements have similar atomic radii and formation enthalpies such that entropy effects dominate.
Changes in atmosphere or pressure can substantially modify synthesis kinetics and cause deviations from the proposed relationship.
